newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila ready to raise rates again if peso attacked.
newsitem.headline: Manila ready to raise rates again if peso attacked.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it was prepared to boost interest rates again to protect the peso and called the latest rise in overnight rates a preemptive move in case there is any spillover from the problems in Thailand.
"We will continue to raise interest rates if there will be speculation on the peso," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters.
The bank earlier raised overnight interest rates by 0.75 percentage points to 12 percent.
"This is just a preemptive action in view of what has happened in Thailand. We don't want a spillover in the Philippines," Edeza said.
The Thai baht was hit by speculative attacks on Wednesday triggered by the country's mounting economic uncertainties.

The Bank of Thailand teamed up with the Monetary Authority of Singapore on Wednesday to defend the baht against fresh market attacks, and Thailand's central bank warned other measures would be taken as necessary to counter market pressure on the currency.
